newsitem.title: USA: First Chicago NBD to buy back 40 mln shares.
newsitem.headline: First Chicago NBD to buy back 40 mln shares.

text.p: First Chicago NBD Corp said Tuesday its board of directors authorized the purchase of up to 40 million shares of the bank holding company's common stock over the next two to three years.
Purchases will occur from time to time in open market or private transactions.
At September 30, 1996, First Chicago NBD had 318 million shares outstanding.

Earlier Tuesday, First Chicago NBD reported 1996 third quarter earnings of $358 million or $1.08 per fully diluted share after a one-time charge of $18 million or $0.04 a share for the recapitalization of the Savings Association Insurance Fund. In the 1995 quarter, the company earned $1.06 a share.

"The quality of this quarter's earnings is the best since the announcement of our merger," said Chairman Verne Istock. "Growth in net interest income and focused expense management continue to boost earnings. Also, credit card charge-offs stabilized relative to the second quarter, and the Bankcard business turned in near-record profits for the quarter."

The company said it completed well ahead of schedule its $25 billion asset reduction program related to the November 1995 merger of First Chicago Corp and NBD Bancorp. First Chicago NBD's assets stood at $106.69 billion at September 30, 1996, down from $124.06 billion at the same time last year.

Operating expenses of $798 million for the third quarter, excluding the SAIF charge, were the lowest in six quarters, it said. Operating expenses for the nine months of 1996 were about flat with the year-earlier period. This resulted from expense reduction actions associated with the merger.
Total market-driven revenue for the third quarter was $40 million, well below the company's $111 million average reported over the past six quarters, it said.

Combined trading activities posted a loss of $12 million. Improving the execution in the capital markets businesses is a top priority in the refocusing of the corporate and institutional banking segment, First Chicago NBD said.
Net interest income was $967 million for the third quarter, up 17 percent from the year-ago quarter.
Noninterest income was $597 million for the third quarter, versus $702 million in the 1995 third quarter.
The provision for credit losses was $185 million for the third quarter, the same as the second quarter and up from $125 million for the third quarter of 1995.
Shares of First Chicago NBD were trading up 5/8 to 47-1/4.
